articles.title: Sri Lanka eyes new job opportunities in Türkiye as Deputy Minister visits Ankara
articles.text:
Deputy Minister Arun Hemachandra will undertake an official visit to Ankara, Türkiye, from October 26 to 28, 2026, to strengthen bilateral relations and expand cooperation in foreign employment, trade, investment, agriculture, tourism and air connectivity.
During the visit, Hemachandra is scheduled to hold discussions with senior Turkish government officials, including the deputy ministers of foreign affairs, labour and social security, trade, and culture and tourism.
Exploring employment opportunities for Sri Lankan workers will be a key priority, with particular emphasis on ethical recruitment and worker protection.
Two bilateral instruments are scheduled to be signed during the visit: a Memorandum of Understanding on Agricultural Cooperation and a protocol amending the Air Transport Agreement between Sri Lanka and Türkiye to strengthen air connectivity.
Hemachandra will also engage with the Ankara Chamber of Commerce to explore opportunities for expanding trade, attracting investment and strengthening partnerships between businesses in the two countries.
The visit forms part of the Sri Lankan government’s broader efforts to strengthen economic diplomacy and diversify international partnerships.
articles.summary: Deputy Minister Arun Hemachandra will undertake an official visit to Ankara, Türkiye, from October 26 to 28, 2026, to strengthen bilateral relations and expand cooperation in foreign employment, trade, investment, agriculture, tourism and air connectivity. Hemachandra will also engage with the Ankara Chamber of Commerce to explore opportunities for expanding trade, attracting investment and strengthening partnerships between businesses in the two countries.

articles.title: Springfield College Kandy Crowned All Island Western Music and Dance Champions 2026
tags: All-Island Western Music and Dance Competition 2026
articles.text:
The Western Junior Choir of Springfield College, Kandy, has emerged as the national champion at the All-Island Western Music and Dance Competition 2026, organised by the Ministry of Education.
The victory marks a proud milestone for the college, reflecting the talent, dedication and teamwork of its young choristers.
The choir’s journey to the championship began in early June, when the students embarked on an intensive programme of rehearsals in preparation for the competition. Through consistent practice, discipline and a shared passion for music, the young performers worked tirelessly to perfect their vocal harmony and presentation.
Their efforts first earned them first place at the provincial-level competition , securing their place at the all-island finals. Building on this success, the choir continued to refine its performance, demonstrating remarkable commitment and perseverance as it prepared to compete against the best in the country.
At the national competition, the Springfield choristers impressed the judges and audience with their performance, ultimately securing first place and winning the championship trophy.
This achievement is a testament not only to the musical ability of the students but also to the guidance and dedication of their teachers-in-charge, the encouragement of the Principal and staff, and the support of parents and well-wishers.
The historic victory has brought immense pride to the Springfield College community, highlighting the importance of nurturing artistic talent and providing students with opportunities to excel beyond the classroom.
The Western Junior Choir’s success stands as a celebration of the power of teamwork and the unifying spirit of music, with the students’ individual voices coming together to create one glorious harmony.
articles.summary: The Western Junior Choir of Springfield College, Kandy, has emerged as the national champion at the All-Island Western Music and Dance Competition 2026, organised by the Ministry of Education. The Western Junior Choir’s success stands as a celebration of the power of teamwork and the unifying spirit of music, with the students’ individual voices coming together to create one glorious harmony.

articles.title: Gateway Graduate School Research Symposium 2026 to Unite Educators, Researchers and Young Innovators
articles.text:
Gateway Graduate School is set to host its Research Symposium 2026 on Saturday, 31 October 2026, at the Bandaranaike Memorial International Conference Hall (BMICH), Colombo, bringing together academics, researchers, educators, policymakers, postgraduate students and school students for a day of intellectual exchange and discovery.
Held under the theme “Research and Innovation in Diverse Global Education,” the Symposium aims to foster a strong research culture, encourage interdisciplinary collaboration and provide a platform for sharing findings and exploring innovative approaches to contemporary educational challenges.
Distinguished International Keynote Speakers
A key highlight of the Symposium will be the participation of two distinguished keynote speakers.
Dr. Harsha Athurupana, Lead Economist at the World Bank , will share insights drawing on his extensive experience in education policy, economic development and educational reform.
Dr. Rozi Binte Rahmat, Lecturer in Education at the College of Human Sciences and Culture, Flinders University, Australia , will contribute perspectives from her academic and research experience in contemporary education.
Five Research Tracks Exploring Educational Challenges
The Symposium will feature parallel research presentations organised under five specialised tracks covering key areas shaping the future of education:
AI, Data & Emerging Educational Technologies: Exploring the role of artificial intelligence, data and emerging technologies in transforming education.
Educational Psychology and Wellbeing: Examining learner development, mental health, wellbeing and supportive learning environments.
Leadership, Policy & Governance: Addressing educational leadership, institutional management and effective governance.
Action Research and Community Engagement: Highlighting research that connects academic knowledge with practical solutions and community development.
Teaching, Learning and Assessments: Exploring innovative teaching approaches, learning strategies and assessment practices.
These sessions will provide opportunities for researchers and practitioners to present their findings, exchange perspectives and explore the practical application of research.
Engaging Discussions with Leading Academics
The Symposium will also feature a panel discussion comprising Prof. Prasad Sethunga, Mr. SanthushWeeraman, Mrs. Vishaka Nanayakkara, Dr. Rozi Binte Rahmat and Mrs. Nirmali Wickremesinghe .
Open to all participants, the discussion will encourage meaningful dialogue on educational research, innovation and emerging challenges, drawing on the diverse expertise and experiences of the panellists.
Inspiring the Next Generation of Researchers
A distinctive feature of the Symposium is its dedicated Student Research Track and Workshop , aimed at introducing school students to academic research and encouraging critical thinking, creativity and independent inquiry.
Under the theme “School Research & Innovation,” students will have an opportunity to showcase their research, present ideas and develop confidence in communicating their findings.
A special workshop titled “The Research Mindset: Preparing for University and Beyond” , facilitated by Mr. Vidujith Vithanage, Visiting Faculty Member and Multidisciplinary Researcher, will help students develop essential research and analytical skills while preparing them for the academic demands of higher education.
Advancing Research and Innovation
The Gateway Graduate School Research Symposium 2026 seeks to strengthen connections between academic research and professional practice while encouraging collaboration among educational institutions, researchers and practitioners.
At a time when education is evolving rapidly in response to technological advancements and changing global needs, the Symposium highlights the importance of evidence-based approaches in shaping educational progress.
By bringing together established academics, emerging researchers and young innovators, Gateway Graduate School hopes to inspire a culture of inquiry that extends beyond classrooms and institutions, encouraging research that contributes meaningfully to education and society.
For registrations and further information, contact Ms. Isuri Kathriarachchi, Conference Secretary , on +94 76 425 6356 or via isuri.kathriarachchi@gateway.lk .
articles.summary: Gateway Graduate School is set to host its Research Symposium 2026 on Saturday, 31 October 2026, at the Bandaranaike Memorial International Conference Hall (BMICH), Colombo, bringing together academics, researchers, educators, policymakers, postgraduate students and school students for a day of intellectual exchange and discovery.

articles.title: Nearly 200 raids : CAA cracks down on shops hiding prices from customers
articles.text:
The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has conducted nearly 200 special raids across Sri Lanka over violations of consumer protection laws, including the failure to display prices of goods offered for sale.
According to the CAA, the raids and market inspections were carried out from October 20 to 24, 2026, across several districts as part of a special enforcement programme aimed at ensuring price transparency and preventing unfair trading practices.
Officials inspected businesses selling rice, sugar, dhal, vegetables, fruits, wheat flour, bakery products, clothing, electrical appliances, mobile phone accessories and other consumer goods.
Violations were detected in several districts, including Galle, Matara, Hambantota, Jaffna, Ampara, Batticaloa, Anuradhapura, Kurunegala, Puttalam, Kandy, Ratnapura and Trincomalee.
The CAA said several businesses had failed to display the prices of essential food items, particularly rice, sugar, dhal, vegetables and fruits.
Legal action has been initiated against the businesses concerned, while dates have been scheduled for filing cases before Magistrates’ Courts in certain instances.
Special investigations were also conducted into wheat flour sales, market availability, stock levels and compliance with pricing regulations.
Under Section 26(1) of the Consumer Affairs Authority Act, No. 9 of 2003, traders are required to clearly display the prices of goods offered for sale where prices are not already marked on the products or their packaging in accordance with the law.
The CAA has urged traders to comply with price display regulations and other consumer protection laws.
Members of the public have also been encouraged to report businesses that fail to display prices or engage in unfair trading practices by contacting the CAA hotline on 1977 during office hours.
articles.summary: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has conducted nearly 200 special raids across Sri Lanka over violations of consumer protection laws, including the failure to display prices of goods offered for sale.

articles.title: Sri Lanka records lowest hunger levels among South Asian nations
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has recorded the lowest hunger index score among South Asian countries with available data in the 2026 Global Hunger Index (GHI), reflecting a significant improvement in the country’s hunger situation over the past two decades.
According to the report released on October 14, Sri Lanka recorded a score of 10.2, placing it 53rd among 122 countries assessed globally.
Among South Asian countries, Nepal recorded the second-lowest score of 14.5, followed by Bangladesh at 19.2, India at 24.1, Pakistan at 25.5 and Afghanistan at 28.6.
The report did not assign scores to Bhutan and the Maldives due to insufficient data.
Sri Lanka’s hunger index score has declined from 22.1 in 2000 to 19.9 in 2006, 20.8 in 2012, 11.4 in 2018 and 10.2 in 2026.
Despite the improvement, Sri Lanka remains in the moderate hunger category, indicating that food security and nutrition challenges persist.
The report also revealed that 4.9% of Sri Lanka’s population is undernourished, while 10.1% of children under five are stunted and 9.3% suffer from wasting. The under-five mortality rate stands at 0.6%.
The Global Hunger Index measures hunger using four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality. Lower scores indicate less severe hunger.
Globally, the 2026 report warned that hunger has begun rising again following nearly two decades of progress, driven by conflicts, climate shocks and economic crises.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka has recorded the lowest hunger index score among South Asian countries with available data in the 2026 Global Hunger Index (GHI), reflecting a significant improvement in the country’s hunger situation over the past two decades. Among South Asian countries, Nepal recorded the second-lowest score of 14.5, followed by Bangladesh at 19.2, India at 24.1, Pakistan at 25.5 and Afghanistan at 28.6.

articles.title: Muslim World League condemns Houthi missile attacks targeting Mecca and Medina regions
articles.text:
The Muslim World League (MWL) has strongly condemned Houthi missile attacks targeting the Mecca and Medina regions of Saudi Arabia, expressing full solidarity with the Kingdom.
In a statement issued on October 25, the organisation denounced the attacks, describing them as a serious violation of the sanctity of Islamic holy sites.
According to the Saudi Press Agency, MWL Secretary-General Sheikh Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulkarim Al-Issa condemned the attacks and reaffirmed the organisation’s support for Saudi Arabia in protecting its territory, civilians and religious sites.
Saudi reports indicated that missile debris had fallen in several locations, including areas near Mecca, Jeddah, Taif and Rabigh.
The Muslim World League expressed its solidarity with Saudi Arabia and supported measures taken by the Kingdom to safeguard its security and stability.
The condemnation follows reports of Houthi missile activity targeting western Saudi Arabia, raising security concerns around the country’s holy cities.
articles.summary: The Muslim World League (MWL) has strongly condemned Houthi missile attacks targeting the Mecca and Medina regions of Saudi Arabia, expressing full solidarity with the Kingdom. The Muslim World League expressed its solidarity with Saudi Arabia and supported measures taken by the Kingdom to safeguard its security and stability.

articles.title: Indian and Sri Lankan Navy bands to perform together at Galle Face Green
articles.text:
The Indian and Sri Lankan Navy bands will hold a joint musical performance at Galle Face Green in Colombo on Tuesday, October 27, as part of the visit of Indian naval ships to Sri Lanka.
According to the Indian High Commission in Colombo, the event will begin at 5 p.m. and feature a joint performance by musicians from the two navies.
The performance is being organised to mark the visit of the Indian Navy’s First Training Squadron (1TS), comprising INS Tir, INS Sujata and Indian Coast Guard Ship (ICGS) Sarathi, to Colombo.
The Indian High Commission has invited members of the public to attend the event, describing it as an evening of music and camaraderie.
The joint performance will provide an opportunity for the public to witness musical presentations by the naval bands of both countries.
articles.summary: The Indian and Sri Lankan Navy bands will hold a joint musical performance at Galle Face Green in Colombo on Tuesday, October 27, as part of the visit of Indian naval ships to Sri Lanka.

articles.title: El Niño’s long shadow: Why 2027 is the year to worry about
articles.text:
By 𝑅𝑜𝑠ℎ𝑒𝑛 𝐹𝑒𝑟𝑛𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑜, 𝐴sian Development Bank 𝐸𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑜𝑚𝑖𝑠𝑡.
El Niño is already at record strength for this time of year and still building. It is expected to peak around November, with a high chance of becoming the strongest on record. Most attention will focus on the coming months: failed rains, heatwaves, and rising rice and cooking oil prices. But the bigger economic story comes later.
El Niño hits hardest in the year after it forms, putting 2027 in the firing line. The usual view is that it delivers a sharp but brief blow to growth, after which economies bounce back.
Recent research suggests otherwise: in hot, dry economies, El Niño can slow productivity growth persistently. The 1997–98 event alone is estimated to have cost the world economy $5.7 trillion in lost output.
𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐝𝐚𝐦𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐦𝐚𝐲 𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐭
Asia and the Pacific are especially vulnerable. Longer-lasting damage is concentrated in tropical economies that are already dry, including many developing economies in the region. In most Southeast Asian economies, farming accounts for 13%–30% of output and 40%–68% of jobs. When harvests fail, poor rural households and women are hit hardest and take the longest to recover. A typical El Niño adds as much as one percentage point to inflation, and more where food makes up a third to almost half of the prices tracked to measure inflation.
A family that sells its livestock, eats its own rice stocks, or takes children out of school to survive a bad year starts the next one poorer and less productive.
Recovery will be harder this time. Many governments carry heavy debt after the pandemic, and countries vulnerable to natural hazards and changing weather patterns already pay more to borrow. Meanwhile, the Middle East conflict, the war in Ukraine, and Red Sea shipping disruptions are straining the food, energy, and freight markets that El Niño will hit.
This shock gives months of warning, unlike most disasters. Governments have time to act. But what would make the biggest difference?
𝐅𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐰𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐦
Line up the money before the shock. Governments can arrange contingent credit lines, catastrophe insurance, and membership in regional risk pools, so money flows quickly once agreed thresholds are crossed. Forecast-based financing releases funds when seasonal forecasts hit pre-set triggers, before the damage arrives. But these tools are often small, cover floods and storms better than drought, and sit outside national budgets. Expanding drought cover and building forecast triggers into government spending would help them work at scale.
Protect the ability to produce, not just consumption. Cash that arrives before harvests fail can reduce the pressure to sell animals, tools, or land, or take children out of school. Food aid keeps families fed. Practical support can keep productive assets working: water and shade for livestock, veterinary checks, drought-tolerant seeds, and planting advice timed to the forecast, and help for fish farmers to change to hardier species.
Switch on social protection early. Adding forecast triggers to existing cash-transfer programs could reach vulnerable groups ahead of the peak, including rural families, women, and informal workers. Release food reserves as prices start climbing, not after they spike. Simple heat-safety measures for outdoor workers, such as adjusted hours, water, and shade, protect both health and incomes.
Keep a steady hand on inflation. When drought pushes up rice or fuel prices, raising interest rates makes borrowing costlier for firms and families already under strain. These price jumps usually fade once supply recovers. The danger is that people expect permanently higher prices and push up wages and other prices in response. Central banks can head this off by explaining that they see the rise as temporary, while making clear they will act if it spreads. Governments can help by avoiding sudden export bans, which push prices up for their neighbors and distort domestic markets. Regional agreement on keeping trade open matters most exactly when markets are tight.
Combine measures rather than choose between them. World Bank analysis focusing on ASEAN economies suggests that bundling interventions can limit losses to gross domestic product far more than any single measure. Financing, farm support, social protection, and clear communication reinforce one another. That argues for one El Niño action plan per country, with governments and development partners working together across Asia and the Pacific, rather than separate responses from separate ministries.
El Niño will come and go within a year.
Whether its damage does, too, depends on what governments do in the next few months. The forecasts are clear enough to act on, the tools are known, and delays now could leave damage that lasts for years. Protecting people’s ability to farm, work, and invest through 2027 is the surest way to keep this El Niño from casting its shadow over the rest of the decade and beyond.
𝑇ℎ𝑖𝑠 𝑏𝑙𝑜𝑔 𝑤𝑎𝑠 𝑤𝑟𝑖𝑡𝑡𝑒𝑛 𝑏𝑦 𝑅𝑜𝑠ℎ𝑒𝑛 𝐹𝑒𝑟𝑛𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑜, 𝐴𝐷𝐵 𝐸𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑜𝑚𝑖𝑠𝑡.
articles.summary: By 𝑅𝑜𝑠ℎ𝑒𝑛 𝐹𝑒𝑟𝑛𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑜, 𝐴sian Development Bank 𝐸𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑜𝑚𝑖𝑠𝑡. El Niño is already at record strength for this time of year and still building.

articles.title: Mandatory vehicle inspections? DMT makes fresh clarification
articles.text:
The Department of Motor Traffic (DMT) has clarified that its proposed roadworthiness and safety certification system is intended only for commercial vehicles used for public transport and the transportation of goods, and not private vehicles.
The clarification follows remarks made by Commissioner General of Motor Traffic, retired Air Marshal Thushara Fernando, regarding plans to introduce mandatory roadworthiness inspections from early 2027.
Speaking at a media briefing on October 22, Fernando said the department was considering introducing a roadworthiness certificate in addition to the existing vehicle emission test certificate.
He also referred to proposals for vehicle inspections at intervals of approximately 5,000 kilometres or three months, with certificates to be issued by authorised garages.
However, his initial remarks did not clearly specify which categories of vehicles would be subject to the proposed requirement.
In a subsequent clarification, the DMT stated that the proposal applies only to commercial vehicles used for passenger and goods transport.
The department emphasised that the proposed system remains under discussion with the Road Worthiness Strategic Committee and that no final decision has been announced on its implementation.
It said the public would be properly informed once the relevant discussions and assessments are completed.
The DMT also urged against circulating misleading information that could create unnecessary confusion among vehicle owners.
The department has yet to announce the final implementation date, inspection criteria and procedures for obtaining the proposed certification.
articles.summary: The Department of Motor Traffic (DMT) has clarified that its proposed roadworthiness and safety certification system is intended only for commercial vehicles used for public transport and the transportation of goods, and not private vehicles. The clarification follows remarks made by Commissioner General of Motor Traffic, retired Air Marshal Thushara Fernando, regarding plans to introduce mandatory roadworthiness inspections from early 2027.

images.alt: Mandatory vehicle inspections? DMT makes fresh clarification

articles.title: Severe lightning alert issued for 4 districts
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has issued an amber advisory for severe lightning in Uva Province and the Ampara and Batticaloa districts, warning residents to take necessary precautions.
According to the advisory issued by the Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre at 11:30 a.m. on Sunday (October 25), thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely at several locations in the affected areas.
The warning remains valid until 11 p.m. on October 25.
The department also warned that temporary, localised strong winds could occur during thundershowers.
Residents have been advised to seek shelter indoors, avoid standing under trees and stay away from open areas such as paddy fields, tea plantations and bodies of water during thunderstorms.
The public has also been urged to avoid using wired telephones, connected electrical appliances and open vehicles, including bicycles, tractors and boats, during thunderstorms.
Authorities have warned residents to remain cautious of fallen trees and power lines.
The Department of Meteorology advised anyone requiring emergency assistance to contact local disaster management authorities.
articles.summary: The Department of Meteorology has issued an amber advisory for severe lightning in Uva Province and the Ampara and Batticaloa districts, warning residents to take necessary precautions. According to the advisory issued by the Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre at 11:30 a.m. on Sunday (October 25), thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely at several locations in the affected areas.

articles.title: Israelis stage mass protest against Netanyahu 3 days before election
articles.text:
Thousands of Israelis gathered in Tel Aviv on Saturday (October 24) to protest against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, just three days before the country’s general election.
The demonstrators demanded an independent investigation into the security failures that allowed the Hamas-led attacks on October 7, 2023, which triggered the war in Gaza.
According to international media reports, protesters assembled at Hostages Square in Tel Aviv, carrying Israeli flags and calling for accountability over the government’s handling of the attacks.
The demonstration was organised by the October Council, a group established by families of people taken captive during the October 7 attacks.
Several prominent opposition figures joined the rally, including Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party and one of Netanyahu’s main political rivals, and Democrats leader Yair Golan.
The October Council has repeatedly called for an independent state commission of inquiry to investigate the circumstances surrounding the attacks and determine responsibility for the security failures.
However, Netanyahu’s government has resisted demands for such an inquiry, proposing instead a commission whose members would be appointed by government and opposition lawmakers.
Opposition leaders have rejected the proposal, arguing that an investigation must be independent of political influence.
The demonstration comes ahead of Israel’s general election scheduled for Tuesday, October 27, with opinion polls suggesting a close contest between Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc and opposition parties.
The election will be Israel’s first general election since the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023.
articles.summary: Thousands of Israelis gathered in Tel Aviv on Saturday (October 24) to protest against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, just three days before the country’s general election. The demonstration comes ahead of Israel’s general election scheduled for Tuesday, October 27, with opinion polls suggesting a close contest between Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc and opposition parties.

images.alt: Israelis stage mass protest against Netanyahu 3 days before election

articles.title: Donkey crossing road leads to fatal Army Defender crash in Mannar
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Police have released further details regarding a fatal accident involving an Army Defender vehicle in Thalaimannar, which claimed the life of a soldier and left 11 others injured.
According to the Police Media Division, the accident occurred on the evening of October 24 along the Mannar–Thalaimannar Road in the Keeriyankudiyiruppu area.
The Defender vehicle, belonging to the Selvari Army Camp, was travelling towards Thalaimannar when a donkey crossed the road.
Police said the driver lost control of the vehicle, causing it to veer off the road and collide with a palm tree.
The driver and 11 Army personnel travelling in the vehicle sustained injuries and were admitted to Pesalai Hospital.
One soldier subsequently succumbed to his injuries, while the remaining 11 injured personnel were transferred to Mannar Hospital for further treatment.
Police identified the deceased as a 42-year-old Army soldier attached to the Selvari Artillery Camp in Thalaimannar and a resident of Nochchiyagama.
Thalaimannar Police are conducting further investigations into the incident.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Police have released further details regarding a fatal accident involving an Army Defender vehicle in Thalaimannar, which claimed the life of a soldier and left 11 others injured. The Defender vehicle, belonging to the Selvari Army Camp, was travelling towards Thalaimannar when a donkey crossed the road.

images.alt: Donkey crossing road leads to fatal Army Defender crash in Mannar

articles.title: Police warn public of scams involving fake dating apps
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Police have urged the public to exercise caution when forming relationships with strangers through dating apps and social media, warning of financial scams involving fraudulent mobile applications.
Several incidents have been reported recently in which scammers use dating apps to establish friendships or romantic relationships with victims, sending attractive messages over short or extended periods to gain their trust and deceive them.
According to police, scammers also approach individuals through social media and messaging platforms such as Facebook, WhatsApp and Telegram, claiming to offer online sexual services or opportunities to form personal relationships. Victims are then persuaded to download and install a specialised mobile application.
Police warned that these applications, which may appear to be dating apps, could be malicious APK files designed to compromise victims’ mobile phones and obtain their online banking credentials.
As a result, scammers may gain access to usernames and passwords associated with victims’ financial accounts when they carry out online transactions while the malicious application remains installed on their devices, enabling the fraudulent withdrawal of funds.
Police said methods used to commit financial fraud through social media and messaging platforms are rapidly evolving, with some scammers exploiting promises of love and companionship to deceive victims and gain access to their financial information.
The public has been urged not to install applications from unknown sources and to avoid sharing banking details, one-time passwords (OTPs), passwords or other personal information with strangers.
Police have also cautioned the public against sharing personal photographs or videos with unknown individuals.
Police stressed that making informed decisions when establishing online relationships is essential to protecting personal safety and financial security, urging the public to remain vigilant when interacting with strangers in the digital environment.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Police have urged the public to exercise caution when forming relationships with strangers through dating apps and social media, warning of financial scams involving fraudulent mobile applications. Police warned that these applications, which may appear to be dating apps, could be malicious APK files designed to compromise victims’ mobile phones and obtain their online banking credentials.

images.alt: Police warn public of scams involving fake dating apps

articles.title: Heavy rain warning issued for several provinces and districts
articles.text:
The Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre has issued an advisory for heavy rain across several parts of Sri Lanka, warning that rainfall exceeding 100 mm is likely in some areas.
The advisory, issued at 5.30 a.m. on Sunday (25), is valid until 5.30 a.m. on Monday (26).
According to the advisory, heavy rainfall exceeding 100 mm is likely at some places in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, North-Western, Northern and Southern provinces, as well as the Kandy, Nuwara Eliya and Anuradhapura districts.
The centre said a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal, near the North Andaman Islands, had intensified into a depression.
Under the influence of this weather system, rainfall is expected to increase across the island over the next few days, starting today (25).
articles.summary: The Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre has issued an advisory for heavy rain across several parts of Sri Lanka, warning that rainfall exceeding 100 mm is likely in some areas. articles.text:

articles.title: Depression in Bay of Bengal expected to intensify into severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday
articles.text:
The low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal in the vicinity of the North Andaman Islands has now intensified into a depression. As of 11.30 p.m. on 24 October 2026, the system was centred near latitude 15.5°N and longitude 91.0°E. The system is very likely to intensify further into a deep depression while moving over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal on 25 October. Continuing to move west-northwestwards, it is very likely to intensify further into a cyclonic storm by the morning of 26 October and into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the morning of 27 October.
Therefore, Naval and fishing communities are warned not to venture to the deep-sea areas bounded by 10N-20N and 80E-95E until further notice. Further, Naval and fishing communities operating in those sea areas are advised to move to safe areas. The naval and fishing communities, are requested to be attentive to the future forecasts and bulletins issued by the Department of Meteorology in this regard.
Condition of Rain: Showers or thundershowers will occur at several places in the sea areas around the island.
Winds: Winds will be South-westerly and Wind speed will be (30-40) kmph. Wind speed can increase up to (50-60) kmph at times in the sea areas off the coast extending from Trincomalee to Pottuvil via Kankasanthurai, Puttalam, Colombo, Galle and Hambantota.
State of Sea: The sea areas off the coasts extending from Trincomalee to Pottuvil via Kankasanthurai, Puttalam, Colombo, Galle and Hambantota will be rough at times. Other sea areas around the island may be fairly rough at times.
The wave height may increase about (2.0 – 2.5) meters in the sea areas off the coast extending from Puttalam to Pottuvil via Colombo, Galle and Matara.
Temporarily strong gusty winds (60-70 kmph) and very rough seas can be expected during thundershowers.
articles.summary: The low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal in the vicinity of the North Andaman Islands has now intensified into a depression.

articles.title: Matara drug haul confirmed at 561.7 kg, valued at over Rs. 11.8 billion
articles.text:
The narcotics seized during a joint Navy and Coast Guard operation at Naotunna Beach in Thalalla, Matara, in the early hours of Saturday (24) have been confirmed to weigh 561.705 kilograms, with an estimated street value of over Rs. 11.8 billion.
Examinations conducted by the Police Narcotics Bureau (PNB) confirmed that the consignment comprised 321.941 kg of heroin and 239.764 kg of crystal methamphetamine, commonly known as Ice.
The drugs were packed in 275 parcels of heroin and 200 parcels of Ice, recovered from nine large polythene sacks, one smaller sack and 11 travel bags found at the scene.
The operation was launched following intelligence received by the Navy and Coast Guard that a consignment of narcotics was being brought ashore in the area.
Upon reaching the location, security personnel observed three individuals attempting to transport a suspicious consignment from a dinghy to the shore. However, the suspects fled before officers could reach them.
Subsequent investigations revealed that the dinghy belonged to a resident of the Devinuwara area. Police searched the owner’s residence but found that he had also fled the area.
Police have identified two suspects in connection with the narcotics consignment. A person suspected of acting as a lookout during the operation was also arrested in the Tangalle area on Saturday, police said.
The seized narcotics were later examined by the Police Narcotics Bureau to establish the exact quantities.
Minister of Public Security Ananda Wijepala, Deputy Minister of Defence Major General Aruna Jayasekara (Retd.) and the Navy Commander were among the senior officials who visited the location to inspect the seized consignment.
Further investigations into the incident are being conducted by the Police Narcotics Bureau.
articles.summary: The narcotics seized during a joint Navy and Coast Guard operation at Naotunna Beach in Thalalla, Matara, in the early hours of Saturday (24) have been confirmed to weigh 561.705 kilograms, with an estimated street value of over Rs. 11.8 billion.

images.alt: Matara drug haul confirmed at 561.7 kg, valued at over Rs. 11.8 billion

articles.title: Sri Lanka to deploy military units to protect endangered wild elephants
articles.text:
The Sri Lankan government has decided to launch a special joint operation involving the Department of Wildlife Conservation and the three armed forces to strengthen the protection of wild elephants and tuskers while addressing human-elephant conflict.
The initiative was discussed at a special meeting held at the Ministry of Environment on October 23, chaired by Environment Minister Dr. Dhammika Patabendi and Deputy Minister Anton Jayakody.
Army Commander Lt. Gen. K. V. Nilantha P. Premaratne, senior wildlife officials, military intelligence and drone operations representatives, and members of environmental organisations, including Wild Tusker, attended the meeting.
Under the proposed programme, a special operations centre will be established at Army Headquarters to coordinate elephant protection activities. Wildlife officers, veterinarians and personnel from the three armed forces will be assigned to the centre.
Authorities have also agreed to introduce special security arrangements for identified tuskers roaming in high-risk areas.
Dedicated Army units will be deployed to monitor their movements and provide protection in vulnerable locations, with particular attention to areas where elephants face threats from illegal activities.
The programme will also strengthen efforts to prevent elephant killings, the use of explosive bait known as hakka patas , and other wildlife crimes.
Joint emergency raids will be intensified in conflict-affected areas, while a reliable intelligence-gathering system will be developed to identify and respond to threats against wildlife.
The meeting also discussed measures to control public gatherings around sick or injured elephants and improve community awareness of wildlife conservation.
Military personnel will receive specialised training from the Department of Wildlife Conservation on handling wild animals and conducting field operations.
Meanwhile, wildlife officers will be provided accommodation at military camps and access to facilities needed for field research and conservation activities.
Authorities have agreed to conduct weekly data reviews to update operational plans, while monthly progress review meetings will be held with key stakeholders.
The Ministry of Environment said the joint programme would be implemented at the ground level as soon as possible, with the objective of protecting wildlife, safeguarding human lives and reducing human-elephant conflict.
articles.summary: The Sri Lankan government has decided to launch a special joint operation involving the Department of Wildlife Conservation and the three armed forces to strengthen the protection of wild elephants and tuskers while addressing human-elephant conflict. Military personnel will receive specialised training from the Department of Wildlife Conservation on handling wild animals and conducting field operations.

articles.title: “Why is he not playing Tests?” Ashwin praises Pavan Rathnayake’s brilliant batting
articles.text:
Former Indian spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has praised Sri Lankan batter Pavan Rathnayake for his impressive strokeplay against England during Sri Lanka’s historic ODI victory in Rawalpindi, while questioning why the youngster has yet to receive an opportunity in Test cricket.
Rathnayake scored a brilliant 130 off 106 deliveries, including 15 fours and three sixes, helping Sri Lanka successfully chase a target of 430 against England on October 22.
Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, winning by two wickets with one ball remaining. Rathnayake was named Player of the Match.
Speaking on his cricket programme, Ashwin said he had watched highlights of Rathnayake’s innings and was impressed by the young batter’s technique, shot selection and ability to play spin bowling.
“He plays spin superbly. Look at the way he was taking on Liam Dawson, hitting him through extra cover,” Ashwin said.
Ashwin also discussed Rathnayake’s approach against England’s pace attack, particularly Jamie Overton.
“When Jamie Overton was bowling early on, he got a little high on the ball while playing the pull shot,” he observed.
Despite that observation, Ashwin was impressed by Rathnayake’s overall batting performance and described Sri Lanka’s emerging batting talent as encouraging.
“I watched some of his highlights. Suddenly, Sri Lanka is producing a lot of exciting batting talent. It is very, very promising for them,” Ashwin said.
He also admitted that Sri Lanka’s successful pursuit of England’s massive total had surprised him.
“Honestly, nobody expected Sri Lanka to chase that target. I certainly didn’t expect it,” he said.
Ashwin compared Sri Lanka’s emergence of promising batters with the challenges Australia has faced in developing consistent batting talent.
“We were just talking about Australia not producing enough batting talent, and suddenly Sri Lanka is bringing through players like Sonal Dinusha, Pavan Rathnayake,” he said.
The former Indian spinner also questioned why Rathnayake had not been selected for Test cricket despite his impressive first-class performances.
Highlighting the batter’s domestic record, Ashwin noted that Rathnayake had scored more than 4,200 runs in 64 first-class matches at an average of nearly 50, including a highest score of 240.
He particularly praised Rathnayake’s first-class strike rate of approximately 67, describing him as a busy batter capable of rotating the strike consistently.
Ashwin suggested that Rathnayake’s ability to score at a healthy rate, combined with his consistency in domestic cricket, made him a strong candidate for Sri Lanka’s Test team.
He also raised concerns about Sri Lanka’s management of talented players, suggesting that uncertainty over selection and inconsistent opportunities could affect their confidence and development.
Ashwin said Sri Lanka possesses considerable batting talent but needs to ensure promising players receive appropriate opportunities to develop at the international level.
Rathnayake’s century was central to Sri Lanka’s remarkable victory after England posted 429 for four, powered by captain Harry Brook’s record-breaking 202.
Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka contributed 97 runs each, while Janith Liyanage struck an unbeaten 61 off 27 balls, including the winning six, to complete the historic chase.
articles.summary: Former Indian spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has praised Sri Lankan batter Pavan Rathnayake for his impressive strokeplay against England during Sri Lanka’s historic ODI victory in Rawalpindi, while questioning why the youngster has yet to receive an opportunity in Test cricket. Despite that observation, Ashwin was impressed by Rathnayake’s overall batting performance and described Sri Lanka’s emerging batting talent as encouraging.

articles.title: OSC Secures Fourth International ARC Award with Bronze Win for Cultivating Change, Inspiring Futures
articles.text:
Four international wins. One evolving story. And another proud moment for The Overseas School of Colombo.
The Overseas School of Colombo (OSC) has once again been recognised on the global stage, earning Bronze at the prestigious International ARC Awards for its 2024/25 annual report, Cultivating Change, Inspiring Futures. The accolade marks OSC’s fourth ARC Award recognition – a milestone that celebrates not only the quality of the publication, but the remarkable community and stories at its heart.
Celebrating its landmark 40 th year in 2026, the International ARC Awards, organised by MerComm, Inc., is the world’s largest annual report competition and is widely regarded as the “Oscars of Annual Reports”. Presented at a gala celebration in New York City, the awards recognise excellence in annual reporting, corporate communication, creativity and transparency among organisations around the world. Past winners have included global names such as PepsiCo, McDonald’s, IBM, The Coca-Cola Company, Nike, Boeing and BMW, placing OSC among an extraordinary international field.
For OSC, however, an annual report has never been simply a collection of achievements, statistics and growth metrics. It is something beyond the numbers and accolades: an opportunity to capture an actual year in the life of the school – the ideas explored, challenges embraced, progress made and the people who are at its epicentre who continue to move the community forward.
“Recognition at the ARC Awards for a fourth time is incredibly meaningful for OSC, particularly because our Annual Report has never simply been about documenting a year of achievements,” said Jehan de Silva, Director of Marketing and Communications at The Overseas School of Colombo. “It is about telling the story of our school with honesty, creativity and purpose, while holding ourselves to the highest standards of transparency and communication. To have that work recognised on the global stage, alongside some of the world’s most respected organisations, is something our entire community can take great pride in.”
At the heart of this award-winning story is a simple but powerful idea: growth must be cultivated .
The theme Cultivating Change, Inspiring Futures. takes inspiration from the tea plant – deeply rooted in Sri Lanka’s landscape and history, yet also a compelling symbol of patience, resilience, care, and renewal.
For OSC, that symbolism reaches even deeper.
The tea plant creates a bridge between the school’s earliest roots in Sri Lanka’s hill country, the extraordinary sustainability journey unfolding across OSC today, and the young people being prepared to inherit and shape the world of tomorrow. Its journey from tender sapling to flourishing plant also echoes the experience of a child at OSC: nurtured within the right environment, encouraged to explore and grow, and gradually developing the confidence and resilience to flourish.
“The tea plant gave us a powerful connection between OSC’s earliest roots in Sri Lanka’s hill country, the extraordinary sustainability work taking place across our school today, and our responsibility to the generations that will follow us,” Jehan explained. “Like education itself, meaningful growth doesn’t happen overnight. It requires patience, care, the right environment and people who are prepared to nurture it.”
That philosophy can be seen across the OSC campus.
As an Eco-School, sustainability is not treated as an occasional campaign or conversation. It is woven through learning, student action and everyday school culture, giving students opportunities to understand that meaningful change can begin with the choices they make within their own community.
OSC’s sustainability journey has also earned the institution the Eco-Schools Green Flag Award, the Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools (MSA-CESS) Programme of Distinction in Sustainability, and recognition as a UNESCO Greening Education Partnership exemplar.
These achievements give Cultivating Change, Inspiring Futures. its substance. The theme is not simply a creative metaphor; it reflects something already taking root across the school.
Established in 1957, OSC is Sri Lanka’s only International Baccalaureate (IB) Continuum School and today brings together a vibrant community representing more than 40 nationalities. Across generations, its story has continued to evolve while remaining grounded in learning, international mindedness, community and a responsibility to the world beyond the classroom.
The ARC Awards celebrate excellence in annual reporting and institutional communications among organisations around the world. A fourth award is therefore a proud milestone for OSC, but the recognition ultimately belongs to the community whose work, ideas and experiences fill the pages of its annual report.
“What makes this Bronze award so meaningful is the story behind it. Our Annual Report, Cultivating Change, Inspiring Futures. , celebrates a school deeply rooted in Sri Lanka, where students, teachers, staff and parents are working together to create a more sustainable future,” said Nel Capadona, Head of School at The Overseas School of Colombo. “To have their efforts recognised on the international stage is something we can all be proud of.”
For OSC, four wins on the global stage are cause for celebration. But perhaps the greater triumph lies in what those awards continue to recognise: a school unafraid to grow, a community determined to make a difference, and generations of young people being given the roots to belong – and the compassion, courage, and curiosity to reach far beyond them.
Cultivating Change, Inspiring Futures. may tell the story of one remarkable year. Yet its real promise lies in all the stories still waiting to flourish and grow.
articles.summary: Four international wins. The Overseas School of Colombo (OSC) has once again been recognised on the global stage, earning Bronze at the prestigious International ARC Awards for its 2024/25 annual report, Cultivating Change, Inspiring Futures.

articles.title: 80 Sri Lankan government websites face potential cybersecurity risks, researcher warns
articles.text:
Unpatched, and unsupported: Sri Lanka’s government websites after PHP2Shell
By Dr Sanjana Hattotuwa
This morning I wrote to the Prime Minister, Dr Harini Amarasuriya, and the Leader of the Opposition, Sajith Premadasa, about 80 websites run by the Sri Lankan state, or by the utilities and companies it owns, that I found running software the world’s leading cybersecurity agencies have told every organisation to fix immediately or take offline, spanning ministries, provinces, municipal councils, the health sector and, most worryingly, institutions that form part of the country’s critical national infrastructure. 61 of the 80 – over three quarters – run versions so old that the makers stopped fixing them years ago, which means the websites, and all their content were exposed to cybercriminals, and other unauthorised domestic, and foreign entities long before this week’s alarm, and remain exposed now with no official repair available. Sri Lanka’s digitalisation foundations remain incredibly weak, and potentially severely compromised.
Engines nobody services
The software generating headlines this week was PHP, an engine of sorts that assembles the pages visitors see on around 70% of the world’s websites. On 21 October its developers disclosed 2 severe defects, since nicknamed PHP2Shell, that could let a stranger on the internet, with no password, take control of the computer behind a website. The US National Security Agency told organisations unable to fix their systems to take them offline, and the South African Presidency, the Finnish government and the UK government did exactly that, since attempts to exploit the flaws began 4 days before they were made public and climbed to millions within a day.
Sites on supported versions can be made safe with an update, whereas sites on retired versions cannot, much as a carmaker eventually stops issuing recalls for a model it no longer builds, and some Sri Lankan state sites run versions abandoned more than a decade ago, so they carry every flaw found since, not just this week’s. I could only count sites that publicly reveal their software version, so 80 is a floor rather than a total, and a site that hides its version tells us nothing about whether it has been patched.
Data, disinformation and critical infrastructure
Several of the exposed systems aren’t just front-facing sites but working applications holding information about citizens and public servants, including health sector staff systems, a portal where doctors log in with their national identity card numbers, and systems linked to the identity registry itself, which sits uneasily with the duty the Personal Data Protection Act places on public authorities to keep personal data secure. Given Sri Lanka’s long and recent history of false information driving offline harm, a compromised official website is also the most credible vehicle for disinformation imaginable, since a forged flood warning, a fake government circular or a falsified tariff notice would be believed precisely because of where it appeared.
The sites belonging to critical national infrastructure (CNI), spanning electricity, ports, telecommunications, transport, disaster management, national identity and defence, are the most concerning. I cannot say whether these websites connect to the billing, grid, port or network systems behind them, but this is exactly the question Parliament should ask, since attackers rarely stop at the website. To wit, even as Japan’s SoftBank suspended its critical earthquake and tsunami alerts this week while it secured its systems, Sri Lanka’s disaster response runs its public website on, incredibly, software more than a decade old.
A government that asks citizens to trust it with their identity, health records and payments online can’t leave its own front doors in this condition.
The official response so far
SL-CERT issued a general advisory on 21 October urging institutions to patch or restrict access, which was the right advice, though it named no institution, and I can find no public evidence that anyone in government has since checked which state websites are affected, told the institutions concerned, set a deadline or taken a single site offline. We have been here before, in August 2023, when a ransomware attack on the Lanka Government Cloud destroyed 3 months of email across an estimated 5,000 government accounts after an upgrade from obsolete software had been delayed since 2021, and 3 years on, 61 government websites show how little has been learnt about abandoned software, which, left running because upgrading is nobody’s priority, nobody’s budget line and nobody’s brief, will eventually be found.
Hours, weeks and months
I urged the Prime Minister to direct every affected institution, within 48 hours, to install the fix or switch on temporary protections, and to take its site offline if it can do neither. Within a week, each should check whether it has already been compromised, and SL-CERT should publish the institutions it has notified, their progress, and a fresh scan of every government website, including those that hide their versions. Every site on retired software should move to a supported version or close within 3 months, a question of budget and accountability rather than technical effort, which is why it belongs in Parliament.
The government is pressing ahead with digitalisation at speed, from the Sri Lanka Unique Digital Identity (SL-UDI) scheme to GovPay for state services, each asking citizens to entrust the state with more of their personal information than ever before, and digital ambition built on this foundation is risk dressed as modernisation, transferred quietly from the state to its citizens, on official websites that remain – as far as anyone outside government can tell – unpatched and unchecked.
articles.summary: Unpatched, and unsupported: Sri Lanka’s government websites after PHP2Shell By Dr Sanjana Hattotuwa This morning I wrote to the Prime Minister, Dr Harini Amarasuriya, and the Leader of the Opposition, Sajith Premadasa, about 80 websites run by the Sri Lankan state, or by the utilities and companies it owns, that I found running software the world’s leading cybersecurity agencies have told every organisation to fix…

articles.title: Sri Lanka explores startup collaboration with IIT Delhi
articles.text:
Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe visited the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi on October 24 to explore opportunities for strengthening Sri Lanka’s startup ecosystem through collaboration with India.
During the visit, discussions focused on India’s experience in developing startup incubation programmes, including the legal and institutional frameworks, support for early-stage businesses and partnerships with the private sector.
According to Abeysinghe, IIT Delhi receives more than 25,000 applications annually, while its incubation programme supports approximately 1,500.
He said the scale of the programme offers valuable lessons on how universities can connect research, talent, industry and investment to develop successful startups.
The discussions also explored potential collaboration between IIT Delhi and Sri Lanka’s startup ecosystem, including knowledge sharing, institutional partnerships and opportunities for Sri Lankan entrepreneurs.
The Deputy Minister said he also had the opportunity to interact with several startups developing innovative solutions with the potential to make a global impact.
“There is much we can learn from India’s experience as we work towards building a more dynamic, innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem in Sri Lanka,” he said.
Sri Lanka’s High Commissioner to India, Mahishini Colonne, and Commercial Attaché Kapila accompanied the Deputy Minister during the visit.

articles.title: Built with private donations, free for patients: Rs 350 mn Comfort Care Home opens in Jaffna
articles.text:
A new palliative care centre built at a cost of over Rs. 350 million with contributions from local and overseas donors was opened in Chavakachcheri, Jaffna, on October 24, offering completely free care to patients suffering from serious and life-limiting illnesses.
The facility, named Comfort Care Home, was officially opened by Minister of Health and Mass Media Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa in Sarasalai, Chavakachcheri.
Unlike conventional medical facilities, the centre focuses on providing comfort, pain relief and emotional support to patients facing advanced stages of illnesses, including cancer and organ failure.
The facility features 20 private rooms, pain management services, oxygen therapy, round-the-clock nursing care and a spiritual garden designed to promote patients’ mental well-being.
Patients will also receive nutritious meals based on medical recommendations, with all services provided completely free of charge.
The project was spearheaded by Dr. K. Devakanthan, a retired nephrologist currently residing in the United States, who serves as the founder and chairman of Comfort Care Home.
The centre was developed with financial support from local and international philanthropists and donors.
More than an acre of land required for the project was donated by the family of the late teacher Kanagasabai.
Speaking at the opening ceremony, Minister Jayatissa said that although modern medicine has made significant progress in treating diseases, there are situations where curing an illness is no longer possible.
He stressed that providing pain relief, emotional comfort, dignity and compassionate care to patients in such circumstances remains an essential responsibility of the healthcare system.
The Minister also noted that palliative care facilities could reduce the financial and emotional burden on families while allowing government hospitals to better utilise resources for patients requiring emergency treatment.
He expressed hope that the Comfort Care Home would serve as a model for establishing similar facilities in other parts of Sri Lanka.
The Minister also pledged the Health Ministry’s support for the continued operation of the centre.
Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasekar, Northern Province Governor Nagalingam Vethanayahan, healthcare professionals, project founders and donors attended the opening ceremony.
articles.summary: A new palliative care centre built at a cost of over Rs. 350 million with contributions from local and overseas donors was opened in Chavakachcheri, Jaffna, on October 24, offering completely free care to patients suffering from serious and life-limiting illnesses. The facility, named Comfort Care Home, was officially opened by Minister of Health and Mass Media Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa in Sarasalai, Chavakachcheri.

articles.title: Diplomats and families gather in Colombo to mark International Day of Diplomats
articles.text:
Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath attended a family gathering hosted by Indonesian Ambassador Dewi Gustina Tobing at the Indonesian Embassy in Colombo on October 24 to mark the International Day of Diplomats.
The event brought together members of the diplomatic community in Sri Lanka and their families for a programme featuring sports, games, karaoke and other activities.
Addressing the gathering, Minister Herath highlighted the importance of diplomacy in promoting peace, strengthening international cooperation and fostering mutual understanding among nations.
He said diplomacy was about building bridges, overcoming differences and creating opportunities for dialogue.
The Minister also expressed Sri Lanka’s gratitude to friendly nations and international organisations for their assistance following the devastation caused by Cyclone Ditwah, describing their support as a reflection of international solidarity.
Herath acknowledged the important role played by families in supporting diplomats and said diplomatic relationships became stronger when official ties developed into lasting friendships.
The gathering was hosted by Ambassador Tobing in her capacity as Dean of the Diplomatic Corps in Sri Lanka.
The Foreign Minister thanked the Indonesian Ambassador and her team for organising the event and extended his wishes to diplomats and their families on the occasion.
articles.summary: Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath attended a family gathering hosted by Indonesian Ambassador Dewi Gustina Tobing at the Indonesian Embassy in Colombo on October 24 to mark the International Day of Diplomats. The Foreign Minister thanked the Indonesian Ambassador and her team for organising the event and extended his wishes to diplomats and their families on the occasion.

articles.title: From Economic crisis to recovery: Harin shares Sri Lanka’s experience at India forum
articles.text:
Former Sri Lankan Tourism Minister Harin Fernando delivered a keynote address at the NavaDisha Global Dialogue on Justice and Reintegration, held at EMIR Business School in Karnataka, India, on October 23, highlighting youth empowerment, economic recovery and the importance of stronger India-Sri Lanka relations.
Speaking on the theme “Youth Crime Prevention and Rehabilitation – A Sustainable Future,” Fernando warned that growing youth frustration, unemployment and inequality could threaten social stability unless governments adopted more inclusive policies.
He stressed the importance of involving young people in decision-making, creating employment opportunities and reforming traditional rehabilitation systems to focus on mental health and well-being.
Fernando also highlighted India’s contribution to reviving Sri Lanka’s tourism industry following the country’s economic crisis and emphasised the importance of strengthening bilateral cooperation in tourism, investment, education and innovation.
He said both countries could work together to create opportunities for young entrepreneurs, share expertise and support long-term economic development.
Referring to Sri Lanka’s 2022 economic crisis, Fernando credited former President Ranil Wickremesinghe with restoring stability through economic reforms, securing an International Monetary Fund programme and rebuilding international confidence.
He said the former President had also entrusted several key ministries to younger political leaders during the recovery period.
Fernando acknowledged that difficult economic decisions could carry political consequences, but said democratic transitions were an important part of governance.
“Having done the hard work and handing over the baton democratically is the beauty of governance,” he said, expressing hope that Sri Lanka would continue progressing regardless of which political party was in power.
Addressing youth rehabilitation, Fernando called for greater emphasis on education, vocational training, employment and mental health support rather than relying solely on punitive measures.
He stressed that young people should be directly involved in designing policies intended to address their challenges.
During his visit to Bengaluru, often described as India’s Silicon Valley, Fernando also engaged with youth groups, emerging entrepreneurs and innovators, exploring opportunities for cooperation and knowledge-sharing between India and Sri Lanka.
He also held meetings with senior Indian political and healthcare figures, including Saleem Ahmed, Chairman of the Karnataka Legislative Council, and Dr. C. N. Manjunath, a BJP Member of India’s Parliament representing Bengaluru Rural.
Dr. Manjunath is a prominent cardiologist, Padma Shri awardee and the son-in-law of former Indian Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda.
He previously served as Director of the Sri Jayadeva Institute of Cardiovascular Sciences and Research, a major cardiac care institution that expanded to approximately 2,000 beds during his tenure.
Fernando described his meeting with Dr. Manjunath as productive.
The former Minister also met Dr. B. C. Bhagavan, Vice Chancellor of Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences in Karnataka.
Concluding his keynote address, Fernando called for stronger cooperation between Sri Lanka, India and the Commonwealth to build a sustainable future for young people.
“Don’t burn the future because of the frustration of today — build it. Because no one else will build it for you,” he told the gathering.
articles.summary: Former Sri Lankan Tourism Minister Harin Fernando delivered a keynote address at the NavaDisha Global Dialogue on Justice and Reintegration, held at EMIR Business School in Karnataka, India, on October 23, highlighting youth empowerment, economic recovery and the importance of stronger India-Sri Lanka relations.

articles.title: Reports of President AKD being hospitalised are false: President’s Office
articles.text:
The President’s Office has dismissed reports circulating on social media claiming that President Anura Kumara Dissanayake was admitted to a private hospital following a sudden illness.
In an official statement, the President’s Office clarified that the reports were false and urged the public not to be misled by such claims.
The President’s Office also advised the public to refrain from sharing unverified information on social media without confirming its accuracy through official sources.

In an official statement, the President’s Office clarified that the reports were false and urged the public not to be misled by such claims.

articles.title: Over 475 kg of heroin and Ice seized from Matara beach
articles.text:
The Sri Lanka Navy and Coast Guard have seized more than 475 kg of heroin and crystal methamphetamine (Ice) during a joint operation at Naotunna Beach in Thalalla, Matara.
According to the Navy, the operation was conducted on Saturday (24) following intelligence received by the Sri Lanka Coast Guard.
During the search, officers recovered 10 sacks and 11 travel bags containing suspected narcotics, along with a dinghy believed to have been used to transport the consignment.
Subsequent examinations conducted with the assistance of the Police Narcotics Bureau (PNB) confirmed the presence of more than 200 kg of Ice and 275 kg of heroin.
The seized narcotics and dinghy were handed over to the PNB for further legal proceedings.
Deputy Minister of Defence Aruna Jayasekara and Minister of Public Security Ananda Wijepala, accompanied by Navy Commander Vice Admiral Damian Fernando and other senior officials, inspected the seized consignment.
Speaking during the inspection, Deputy Minister Jayasekara said joint operations by the Navy and Coast Guard had resulted in the seizure of narcotics with an estimated street value of Rs. 97 billion over the past year.
He said operations involving the armed forces, police, Special Task Force and local and foreign intelligence agencies would continue to prevent narcotics from entering Sri Lanka.
The Deputy Minister also urged the public to provide information on drug trafficking through the hotlines 1818 or 1997.
articles.summary: The Sri Lanka Navy and Coast Guard have seized more than 475 kg of heroin and crystal methamphetamine (Ice) during a joint operation at Naotunna Beach in Thalalla, Matara. Subsequent examinations conducted with the assistance of the Police Narcotics Bureau (PNB) confirmed the presence of more than 200 kg of Ice and 275 kg of heroin.

articles.title: Sri Lankan military delegation visits Indian firing range and simulator facilities
articles.text:
A delegation from the Sri Lanka Army’s Regiment of Artillery visited the School of Artillery in Deolali, India, as part of the 11th Army-to-Army Staff Talks (ASST) between the two countries.
According to the Sri Lanka Army, the visit aimed to strengthen professional ties and facilitate the exchange of artillery knowledge, expertise and training practices between the two armies.
During the visit, the delegation toured several key training and operational facilities, including the Faculties of Gunnery, Doctrine and Tactics, the Trials and Technology Wing, the Deolali Field Firing Range, simulator facilities and the Rudranaad Museum.
The visit formed part of ongoing military cooperation between Sri Lanka and India, focusing on professional exchanges and strengthening bilateral defence ties.
articles.summary: A delegation from the Sri Lanka Army’s Regiment of Artillery visited the School of Artillery in Deolali, India, as part of the 11th Army-to-Army Staff Talks (ASST) between the two countries.
